about: How every gun model is held in first person. A model declares only geometry (its right grip; optionally its own left palm, muzzle, SightLook and Magazine; its mesh bounds); these numbers are the one rule for all of them: the size and hold the owner approved on the EnergyLab guns, the hand and reach read from the game. A package's forge-gun-grips table (GunGrips) gives each of its models the preset (below) the game hold is taken from, the muzzle/sight points the model lacks or has in the wrong place, and any per-hand adjustment. A model's own hand sockets are kept (a missing right grip is its origin); a missing left hand is derived from that hold (GunHold.LeftGrip: where the game gun's left palm sits relative to its right palm, on the model's right grip), and the mount pulls the left hand back along the gun into the arm's reach (GunHold.IntoReach). ForgeVisual (GunHold.Solve) reads this file; a website implementation reads the same file and must reproduce gun-hold.cases.json.

length.about: Every model is shown at shownScale of its authored size, never squeezed (models are authored at real-world size, which in first person reads too big next to the game's own guns; 0.85 is the size the EnergyLab guns are approved at). min-max is the shown length along the bore (metres, mesh bounds) of the game's own guns, read in game on 11-05: pistol 0.32 to sniper 1.18 (rifle 0.79, SMG 0.74, machine guns 0.95-0.96, shotgun 1.06). A model outside it is its author's error (visual-gun-size-out-of-range) and keeps its size.

palm.about: Where the palm touches what it holds, in the frame of the game's own hand node (the wrist: -X toward the fingers, +Z toward the thumb, palm -Y left / +Y right, metres): the palm centre read in game on every vanilla gun (G0 readback, the same on all of them: left -6.19, -0.24, 0.06 cm; right -6.22, 0.27, 0.84 cm) plus 1.5 cm along the palm normal to its skin. A model's bare RightHand and LeftHand (no rotation of their own) are the points on the gun where the palm touches: the pistol grip's right side; a fore grip's left side or the handguard's lower left edge, where the game's own hand meets it. The hand keeps the replaced game gun's hand rotation unless the gun's grip table turns it (adjust angle; none of the shipped guns does): the game's grip pose (fingers included) is made for it, and on every vanilla gun (G0) the left palm faces the gun from its lower left, 1-59 degrees above level (rifle 1, pistol 18, sniper 27, machine guns 30-34, SMG 48, shotgun 59), its fingers along the bore, the palm 6-15 cm below the bore and 2-5 cm left of it. Its wrist goes where this point of the hand lands on the model's point. A grip point with its own rotation is the wrist itself (the same convention) and takes no offset. A model's own left socket is kept where it is; where it is missing the mount derives the left point from these palms and the native hold, and when the hip cannot reach that left wrist it pulls the hand back along the gun (reach below).

presets.about: The game's own holds, one per grip animation, read in game (G0) on the game's guns: gear is the offline gear block that holds this way (a new gun borrows its grip to get the hold), leftAnim/rightAnim the grip animations, right/left the hand node (the wrist) in the gun frame (metres; rotation [x, y, z, w]), muzzle and, where read, sight. A gun's grip table (forge-gun-grips) names the preset the model is held by. In game the targets follow the model's own hand points (a missing left hand from the actual gun's own hold) and still take what the actual gun's own hand nodes do on their own; without the game (the website, the shared cases) a preset stands in for them, so GunHold.Solve gives the same wrists whenever the gun holds as its preset says. rifle-2's and machinegun-2's sight come from the donor nodes in gun-hold.cases.json. The rows from rifle-3 on, and rifle-2's muzzle, are read statically from the part prefabs in the game files on 11-08 (hand and muzzle nodes in the part's frame, which is the gun frame): the same read gives the left hand of the seven G0 guns within 0.1 mm and 0 degrees (SMG: 8 mm, 11 degrees) and their muzzles within 0.1 mm. A stock without its own right-hand node gets the grip align it spawns (Default_GripAlign: rifle's right; Stock_Precision_2_GripAlign: rifle-2's right). A website preview finds its preset by the gun's own left grip animation (one preset per animation), so a gun outside these rows previews on the rifle preset with a hint; in game the hands use the actual gun's nodes either way.

hold.about: Added to the replaced gun's hip and relaxed first-person position (metres, the game's item settings frame), and the item camera's hip field of view: halfway between EnergyLab's earlier hold ([0.02, -0.05, 0.14], 45 degrees) and the game gun's own (no offset, its own field of view, 32-36 degrees by kind), as the owner chose on 11-06. The field of view is the game gun's own plus hipItemFovWeight of the way to hipItemFov, to the whole degree the game stores (DMR 32 to 39, machine gun 35 to 40, sniper 34 to 40, rifle 33 to 39). Aiming stays the game's: it lines the model's SightLook up with the camera.

sight.about: The world camera's field of view while aiming through a 1x sight (degrees): the median of the game's own open red-dot and holographic sights (GearSightPart WorldFovZoom 39-50, read from the game's DataBlocks on 11-06; the game's magnified sights are 25, 17 and 17). A ForgeVisual sight (Data/sights.json) of magnification m aims at the field of view whose half-angle tangent is this one's over m (2x: 23 degrees), to the whole degree the game stores; the item camera keeps the game gun's own aim field of view.

reach.about: First-person shoulder (upper arm bone) to a hand target, metres, read in game: the arm is 33 + 29 cm. At the hip the mount pulls the left hand back along the gun until it is in reach (visual-grip-pulled-into-reach, one line for the model's author); the right hand is the model's anchor and over max is still visual-grip-out-of-reach. Over max while aiming, or over near, is a hint.
